9	# Feature Specification: FEAT-004 — Shared Model Catalog and Policy Routing
10	
11	**Feature ID**: FEAT-004
12	**Status**: Draft
13	**Priority**: P0 (provider sources/endpoints), P1 (catalog), P1 (routing)
14	**Owner**: Fizeau Team
15	
16	## Overview
17	
18	Fizeau routes requests by evaluating `route(client_inputs, fiz_models_snapshot)`.
19	Client inputs include policy/profile, pins, `no_remote`, metered opt-in, tools,
20	context, reasoning needs, and other explicit constraints. The `fiz models`
21	snapshot is the only source of routing facts: health, quota, model
22	availability, effective cost, `actual_cash_spend`, billing kind, context/tools/
23	reasoning support, locality, reliability, latency, utilization, and per-field
24	freshness.
25	
26	The snapshot is assembled from configured provider sources and harnesses,
27	discovered model IDs, catalog metadata, and runtime signals joined into one set
28	of provider/model facts. Fizeau has no required daemon. Its freshness contract
29	is cache-first stale-while-revalidate on route hot paths plus explicit blocking
30	refresh surfaces, all sharing cross-process locks, single-flight coalescing,
31	TTLs, cooldowns, bounded concurrency, and atomic snapshot writes. A long-running
32	DDx server may call the same Fizeau refresh entrypoints to keep snapshot facts
33	warm, but route correctness must not depend on that process.
34	
35	The public v0.11 routing surface is:
36	
37	- `Policy`: one of `cheap`, `default`, `smart`, or `air-gapped`;
38	- `MinPower` and `MaxPower`: numeric soft power hints on the 1..10 catalog
39	  scale;
40	- hard pins: `Harness`, `Provider`, and exact `Model`.
41	
42	Deprecated route tables, model reference aliases, compatibility targets, and
43	surface policy projections are not public routing controls.
44	
45	This feature spec defines the required routing behavior and public contracts.
46	`SD-005` owns the implementation sequence, cache mechanics, candidate scoring
47	formula, and routing trace construction.
48	
49	## Problem Statement
50	
51	- Provider config should describe transport/auth, not route policy.
52	- The catalog should own model metadata, power, cost, deployment class,
53	  auto-routable status, and provider surface strings.
54	- Callers need a small, explainable routing vocabulary that avoids accidental
55	  paid spend but still allows exact pins and explicit escalation.
56	
57	## Terminology
58	
59	- **Policy**: a named bundle of power bounds, local allowance, and hard
60	  requirements.
61	- **Power**: catalog model-strength integer from 1 to 10. `0` means unknown or
62	  exact-pin-only.
63	- **Hard pin**: caller assertion on `Harness`, `Provider`, or exact `Model`.
64	- **Route candidate**: one `(harness, provider, endpoint, model)` option after
65	  live discovery and catalog join.
66	- **Default inclusion**: provider-level `include_by_default`, used only for
67	  unpinned automatic routing.
68	- **Metered opt-in**: operator permission for pay-per-token candidates to
69	  participate in unpinned automatic routing. Provider default inclusion is still
70	  required.
71	- **Effective cost**: normalized request-local scoring cost. Subscription
72	  candidates use PAYG-equivalent pricing for comparison even when dispatch does
73	  not create actual cash spend.
74	- **Actual cash spend**: whether dispatching the candidate creates incremental
75	  pay-per-token billing. This is separate from effective cost.
76	- **Unpinned request**: a request with no `Harness`, no `Provider`, and no exact
77	  `Model`. `Policy`, `MinPower`, `MaxPower`, `Reasoning`, capability flags, and
78	  token estimates do not make a request pinned.
79	- **Sticky affinity**: a score bonus for reusing a server instance for related
80	  requests when the candidate is still eligible.
81	
82	## Requirements
83	
84	### Catalog and Manifest
85	
86	1. The manifest schema is v5.
87	2. Catalog models carry concrete model ID, provider surface strings, power,
88	   auto-routable/exact-pin-only status, deployment class, cost, context,
89	   benchmark provenance, capabilities, and reasoning defaults.
90	3. Catalog policies carry `min_power`, `max_power`, `allow_local`, and
91	   `require[]`.
92	4. Catalog providers carry provider `type`, `include_by_default`, and explicit
93	   billing only when the hardcoded provider-system table cannot infer billing.
94	5. Removed v0.10 routing concepts (`target`, aliases as routing personas, and
95	   user-visible `surface_policy`) must not be presented as public routing API.
96	   Narrow compatibility structs may exist only to keep older internal catalog
97	   readers working while the primary v5 shape is used.
98	6. Ordinary execution uses the embedded or configured local manifest. It does
99	   not fetch manifest updates over the network.
100	
101	### Canonical Policies
102	
103	7. The canonical policy set is exactly:
104	
105	| Policy | MinPower | MaxPower | AllowLocal | Require | Intent |
106	|--------|----------|----------|------------|---------|--------|
107	| `cheap` | 5 | 5 | true | none | minimize effective cost; local/fixed candidates preferred |
108	| `default` | 7 | 8 | true | none | balanced default; local/fixed or healthy subscription can win |
109	| `smart` | 9 | 10 | false | none | quality-first; subscription/cloud-capable candidates preferred |
110	| `air-gapped` | 5 | 5 | true | `no_remote` | local-only execution; remote/account providers rejected |
111	
112	8. `ListPolicies` returns these canonical entries and manifest metadata. It
113	   does not list dropped compatibility names.
114	9. `allow_local=false` disallows local/fixed candidates for that policy unless
115	   the caller changes policy or requirements.
116	10. `require[]` currently supports `no_remote`. Unknown requirements fail
117	    validation instead of being ignored.
118	11. `no_remote` rejects remote or account-billed candidates even when the
119	    caller pins a provider or harness.
120	
121	### Assembled Routing Inventory
122	
123	12. `ResolveRoute`, `RouteStatus`, and `fiz models` use the same assembled
124	    snapshot as their routing inventory contract. The router must not maintain a
125	    second discovery view that can diverge from operator-visible model facts.
126	    `ResolveRoute` is the public `route(client_inputs, fiz_models_snapshot)`
127	    contract.
128	13. The assembled snapshot contains one identity per discovered
129	    `(provider, model_id)` pair, including harness-as-provider identities for
130	    subscription harnesses. Catalog-only models do not appear as available
131	    models unless a configured source actually serves them.
132	14. Live discovery wins over configured model hints. A configured default model
133	    is a fallback hint when discovery is unavailable, not a closed inventory.
134	15. Discovered model IDs may be matched to catalog metadata when the mapping is
135	    unambiguous. Unknown models remain inspectable and exact-pinnable, but are
136	    not eligible for unpinned automatic routing.
137	16. The route decision trace records selected, eligible, and rejected
138	    candidates with typed reasons. Consumers must use typed fields, not parse
139	    human-readable reason strings.
140	17. Test-only harnesses never leak into policy-based routing unless explicitly
141	    requested.
142	
143	### Snapshot Freshness
144	
145	18. `fiz models` is quick by default. It reads the current assembled snapshot,
146	    returns available stale data with freshness metadata, and does not block on
147	    slow discovery or runtime probes.
148	19. `fiz models` may request a best-effort background refresh for stale fields,
149	    but only through the same refresh coordinator, cross-process locks, and
150	    single-flight markers used by blocking refresh. A short-lived CLI process
151	    must not spawn independent probe storms or imply that background refresh is
152	    required for correctness.
153	20. `fiz models --refresh` blocks until routing-relevant stale fields have been
154	    refreshed or conclusively failed. `fiz models --refresh-all` blocks on every
155	    refreshable field.
156	21. `ResolveRoute` and `Execute` are cache-first before scoring. They read the
157	    freshest cached routing-relevant facts available for the request: health,
158	    quota, model availability/discovery, context/tool/reasoning support,
159	    billing and effective-cost metadata when dynamic, and utilization when
160	    available. Stale or missing local-provider facts may request a coordinated
161	    asynchronous refresh, but unpinned autorouting and explicit non-local
162	    harness/provider selection must not synchronously contact a local model
163	    provider or block on `/v1/models`. Cached failed probe/discovery evidence
164	    still gates known-dead local providers with typed dispatchability reasons.
165	22. A DDx server or other long-running client may maintain freshness by calling
166	    Fizeau's refresh/warmup entrypoints on a heartbeat. This is an optimization
167	    over the same lock-coordinated cache contract. If no maintainer is running
168	    and `fiz models` observes stale fields, it should expose the stale status
169	    and suggest `fiz models --refresh` or starting a DDx freshness maintainer.
170	
171	### Eligibility and Pins
172	
173	23. Hard pins narrow the candidate set before scoring:
174	    - `Harness` means only that harness may be used.
175	    - `Provider` means only that provider source or selected endpoint may be
176	      used.
177	    - `Model` means only that exact model identity may be used.
178	24. Unpinned automatic routing excludes pay-per-token candidates unless the
179	    provider is included by default and metered routing is explicitly opted in
180	    by user config.
181	25. Pins override provider `include_by_default` and metered opt-in: a
182	    deliberately pinned default-deny pay-per-token provider can be considered.
183	26. Pins do not override policy `require[]`; `air-gapped` plus a remote
184	    provider pin fails.
185	27. Missing-power, inactive, deprecated, and exact-pin-only models are excluded
186	    from unpinned automatic routing. Exact model pins may still use them when
187	    the selected harness/provider can serve the model.
188	28. Hard gates are limited to explicit user constraints and dispatchability:
189	    pins, `require[]`, `no_remote`, metered opt-in, exact-pin support, and
190	    whether the candidate can actually be dispatched. Known-down endpoints,
191	    exhausted quota pools, and missing required context/tools/reasoning support
192	    are dispatchability failures. Cost, quality, non-fatal health risk, latency,
193	    utilization, and power fit are scoring inputs, not broad vetoes.
194	
195	### Power Scoring
196	
197	29. `MinPower` and `MaxPower` are soft scoring hints, not closed candidate
198	    lists, once a model has passed auto-routable eligibility.
199	30. A candidate below `MinPower` receives a stronger penalty than a candidate
200	    above `MaxPower`. This asymmetric scoring reflects failure risk: too weak
201	    is more likely to fail the task, while too strong is primarily a cost and
202	    latency concern.
203	31. If no power hints are supplied, model power contributes positively to the
204	    score alongside policy cost/placement preferences.
205	32. Exact `Model` pins keep exact identity. Policy-derived power bounds are
206	    still reported as evidence, but they do not substitute a different model.
207	
208	### Ranking
209	
210	33. Ranking considers:
211	    - policy baseline (`cheap`, `default`, `smart`, `air-gapped`);
212	    - catalog power;
213	    - provider billing and effective cost;
214	    - subscription shadow cost using PAYG-equivalent effective cost while
215	      retaining `actual_cash_spend=false`;
216	    - subscription quota health and burn-rate prediction;
217	    - route-health cooldown and observed reliability;
218	    - context headroom and required capabilities;
219	    - observed latency/speed;
220	    - endpoint utilization and saturation;
221	    - sticky affinity.
222	34. A qualified candidate is one that passes hard constraints, policy
223	    requirements, default-inclusion and metered opt-in gates, auto-routability,
224	    liveness, quota, and dispatchability. Power hints shape ranking inside that
225	    qualified set rather than replacing exact pins.
226	35. For a given policy and qualified set, Fizeau prefers the lowest effective
227	    cost candidate whose power fit is sufficient for the policy intent.
228	    A zero-cost but substantially underpowered candidate should not beat an
229	    in-band candidate for routine `default` work solely because it is free. A
230	    subscription model may have `actual_cash_spend=false` and still carry a
231	    PAYG-equivalent effective cost for scoring.
232	36. `cheap` selects the lowest effective-cost candidate with enough expected
233	    capability for the request. It should naturally prefer nano, mini, local, or
234	    fixed-cost candidates over maximum-quality frontier models when those
235	    cheaper candidates are available and sufficient; this is a scoring outcome,
236	    not a frontier-model exclusion gate.
237	37. `default` selects a routine balanced candidate. It should avoid maximum
238	    frontier models when lower-cost candidates satisfy the same routing
239	    constraints and expected capability.
240	38. Local/fixed candidates are preferred by `cheap` and `default` when they are
241	    eligible and capable. This preference never beats hard pins or
242	    `require[]`.
243	39. `smart` prefers higher-capability subscription/cloud routes when healthy
244	    and allowed.
245	40. `air-gapped` is local-only through `require=["no_remote"]`.
246	41. If at least one candidate is dispatchable under the user's explicit
247	    constraints, automatic routing must select one candidate even when the
248	    result is imperfect. If user constraints remove all candidates, routing
249	    fails clearly and attributes the failure to those constraints.
250	42. The router dispatches one selected candidate per request. Semantic retry or
251	    escalation belongs to the caller.
252	
253	### Status and Evidence
254	
255	43. `ResolveRoute` returns the selected candidate plus the full candidate
256	    trace, power policy, sticky evidence, utilization evidence, and the selected
257	    model's catalog-projected power.
258	44. `RouteStatus` reports recent decisions, cooldowns, provider reliability,
259	    sticky assignments, and routing-quality metrics. Routing quality is
260	    distinct from provider reliability.
261	45. Session logs and final events record the actual attempted route and failure
262	    class. They use v0.11 `policy` / `power_policy` fields.
263	46. When a route succeeds, fails, or rejects candidates, the evidence must be
264	    explainable from the same assembled snapshot facts exposed by `fiz models`
265	    plus request-local constraints.
266	47. Route evidence records the snapshot version, per-field freshness,
267	    refresh-failure status, effective cost, cost source, billing kind, and
268	    `actual_cash_spend` for selected and rejected candidates.
269	
270	## Acceptance Criteria
271	
272	| ID | Criterion | Suggested Verification |
273	|----|-----------|------------------------|
274	| AC-FEAT-004-01 | The embedded manifest is schema v5 and validates models, policies, providers, billing, and supported requirements. | `go test ./internal/modelcatalog ./...` |
275	| AC-FEAT-004-02 | `ListPolicies` returns exactly `air-gapped`, `cheap`, `default`, and `smart` with power bounds, `allow_local`, `require[]`, and manifest metadata. | `go test ./... -run ListPolicies` |
276	| AC-FEAT-004-03 | `cheap`, `default`, `smart`, and `air-gapped` produce the documented local/subscription/remote behavior under representative inventories. | `go test ./internal/routing ./... -run Policy` |
277	| AC-FEAT-004-04 | Pay-per-token providers are skipped in unpinned automatic routing unless provider default inclusion and metered opt-in both allow them, while explicit pins can select them. | `go test ./... -run 'IncludeByDefault|Metered'` |
278	| AC-FEAT-004-05 | Pins override default inclusion and metered opt-in but not `require[]`; `air-gapped` plus a remote pin returns `ErrPolicyRequirementUnsatisfied`. | `go test ./internal/routing ./... -run Policy` |
279	| AC-FEAT-004-06 | Soft power scoring penalizes undershooting `MinPower` more than overshooting `MaxPower` and does not replace an exact model pin. | `go test ./internal/routing ./... -run Power` |
280	| AC-FEAT-004-07 | Route decisions consume the assembled snapshot, expose typed candidate rejection reasons, score components, selected endpoint/server instance, sticky evidence, and utilization evidence. | `go test ./... -run 'ResolveRoute|RouteStatus|routing_decision|ModelSnapshot'` |
281	| AC-FEAT-004-08 | `ResolveRoute` and `Execute` are cache-first and may request coordinated asynchronous refresh for stale routing-relevant fields, while `fiz models` stays quick by default and `--refresh`/`--refresh-all` block explicitly. | `go test ./internal/discoverycache ./internal/modelregistry ./agentcli ./... -run 'Refresh|Fresh|Models'` |
282	| AC-FEAT-004-09 | Subscription candidates use PAYG-equivalent effective cost for scoring while surfacing `actual_cash_spend=false`; pay-per-token candidates are hard-gated only when dispatch would create actual metered spend without opt-in. | `go test ./internal/routing ./... -run 'EffectiveCost|ActualCashSpend|Metered'` |
283	| AC-FEAT-004-10 | Removed v0.10 names are not advertised by policy listing, CLI help, or public service fields. | `go test ./agentcli ./cmd/fiz ./...` |
284	
285	## Constraints and Assumptions
286	
287	- Fizeau owns routing inside the embedded runtime; callers own semantic retry
288	  and cross-harness orchestration strategy.
289	- Provider configs remain transport/auth definitions.
290	- Catalog data can be refreshed explicitly, but normal request execution is
291	  offline with respect to manifest fetching. Runtime snapshot facts may request
292	  asynchronous refresh before or after autorouting, but route scoring uses cached
293	  evidence and must not block on local provider contact.
294	- Benchmark inputs inform power, but deployment class and cost prevent local
295	  community copies from tying managed frontier models solely on one benchmark.
296	
297	## Dependencies
298	
299	- `FEAT-003` for provider identity, billing, and default inclusion.
300	- `FEAT-005` for cost/session projections.
301	- `FEAT-006` for the CLI surface.
302	- `ADR-009` for the v0.11 naming and migration decision.
303	- `ADR-012` for assembled snapshot cache and harness-as-provider identity.
304	
305	## Out of Scope
306	
307	- User-authored route tables or per-request fallback chains.
308	- Automatic learning from routing-quality metrics.
309	- Network manifest refresh during ordinary execution.
310	
311	## Addendum: tiered, quota-aware routing for cost-efficient consistent progress (2026-05-31)
312	
313	Goal: drain queues with **consistent progress** (beads complete at a predictable
314	rate without exhausting subscription quota before reset), preferring **subscription
315	throughput** over wasted attempts, with **local compute as a non-blocking mixin**.
316	
317	### Subscription tiers (per harness)
318	Each flat-rate subscription harness exposes three tiers:
319	
320	| tier | claude | codex | catalog power | auto-routing |
321	|---|---|---|---|---|
322	| low | haiku | gpt-nano | 7 | **pin-only** (`exact_pin_only`); never auto-selected |
323	| **middle** | sonnet | gpt-5.4-mini | 8 | **default auto-route start** |
324	| max | opus | gpt-5.5 | 10 | escalation target; (later) direct on trusted quota surplus |
325	
326	Cheap work belongs on **local compute**, not a weak subscription tier — a weak
327	subscription tier wastes flat throughput on give-ups. Weak tiers are usable only
328	when explicitly pinned.
329	
330	### Local models = non-blocking, speculative mixin
331	Local (qwen) endpoints are slow/weak and frequently unavailable. They are NOT a
332	primary tier. When healthy, a small sample of low-stakes work may be routed to them
333	**speculatively** to gather usage data: isolated git worktree, hard-kill timeout at
334	the checkout layer, **no durable bead claim until the result validates**, separate
335	metrics namespace, never eligible for dirty/migration/refactor/fragile beads, off the
336	critical path. **INVARIANT (top acceptance test): a local/unavailable/stale provider
337	NEVER gates the candidate set and NEVER blocks subscription routing — provider-down is
338	a clean skip, not a routing failure.**
339	
340	### Quota signal = best-effort telemetry, not a hard control input
341	Subscription quota is observed best-effort (per-response token headers preferred over
342	PTY `/usage` deltas, which are contaminated by concurrent workers + manual CLI + async
343	refresh and lack reliable reset timestamps). A data-quality state machine labels each
344	snapshot `fresh | stale | missing | conflicted | reset_detected`. **When quota is not
345	fresh+attributable, behave conservatively: route MIDDLE, no max-start, no burn-model
346	update.** Burn estimates use conservative percentiles (p75/p90), not mean, with an
347	explicit cold-start prior of "unknown => scarce". (This amends "Out of Scope: automatic
348	learning from routing metrics" — telemetry informs policy but thresholds remain
349	operator/data-tuned, not self-learned closed-loop.)
350	
351	### Escalation: single owner, genuine-failure only
352	There is exactly ONE owner of middle->max escalation; the other layers (fizeau engine
353	ladder, service `escalatePolicyLadder`, ddx power-retry) must not independently
354	escalate tier. Escalation is a single hop, fired ONLY on a typed **genuine
355	implementation/capability failure** classification. A per-pool in-flight max-attempt
356	cap prevents multi-worker stampede onto the max tier.
357	
358	### Failure-classification table (normative)
359	Every attempt outcome maps to exactly one action. ddx and fizeau MUST classify
360	identically against this table:
361	
362	| outcome | action |
363	|---|---|
364	| `success` / `already_satisfied` | close bead |
365	| `no_changes` (agent produced nothing, rationale present) | close or unclaim per rationale; **do NOT escalate tier** |
366	| genuine implementation/capability failure (tests fail after real work; AC unmet) | **escalate middle->max once** |
367	| dirty worktree / partial write | clean/reset worktree, **same-tier retry** (not escalation) |
368	| provider transport failure (i/o timeout, conn refused, 5xx) | **same-tier reroute** to another dispatchable candidate; no tier change |
369	| quota exhausted (`retry_after`) | **global pool cooldown/sleep** until reset; not per-bead mutation, not escalation |
370	| auth/config missing, toolchain/setup failure | **operator-attention** (typed bead state); do not escalate |
371	| timeout / no-progress watchdog | clean + same-tier retry once, then operator-attention |
372	| merge/land conflict | unclaim + retry later; not escalation |
373	| max-tier genuine failure | **operator-attention** (stop escalating) |
374	
375	`operator-attention` = an explicit bead state transition (not a notification or an
376	indefinite queue wait).
377	
378	### Total-subscription-exhaustion behavior
379	Both subscriptions exhausted + local down => **global pool cooldown/sleep** honoring
380	`retry_after`, NOT N per-bead cooldown mutations and NOT spin-polling.
381	
382	### Phasing (reliability first; economics last, telemetry-gated)
383	- **Phase 0 - Foundations:** repo isolation + dirty-repo guard with cleanup/revert
384	  contract; freeze routing replay fixtures (baseline before any change); define the
385	  consistent-progress throughput metric; pick the single escalation owner and freeze
386	  what the other layers must not do.
387	- **Phase 1 - Boring reliable router (first slice):** low tier `exact_pin_only`;
388	  default-start MIDDLE; the local-never-gates invariant + test; the failure-class
389	  table + tests; the single one-hop middle->max retry on typed genuine failure with a
390	  per-pool max-attempt cap; **no max-start / no quota economics yet**; kill-switch
391	  to force a known-good simple policy.
392	- **Phase 2 - Telemetry (best-effort):** header-based burn per (harness,tier); data-
393	  quality state machine; conservative percentiles + cold-start prior; fix codex
394	  `/status` probe and gate codex-pool routing on it (until then codex = unknown=scarce).
395	- **Phase 3 - Quota economics (only once telemetry is trusted):** abundance gate with
396	  two-threshold hysteresis (>60% enter max-start, <40% leave) + minimum dwell; requires
397	  real reset timestamps; cross-pool normalized surplus after reserve + in-flight burn +
398	  escalation budget, sticky primary; E[quota] escalation with double-spend buffer gated
399	  on an INPUT-side difficulty signal.
400	- **Phase 4 - Local mixin:** the speculative/isolated sampling above.
401	- **Phase 5 - Gate-model cleanup:** collapse the ~14 ad-hoc reject gates to
402	  {explicit-constraints, network-dispatchability, capability-dispatchability} + scoring,
403	  behind a kill-switch, with a full gate-mapping table and replay equivalence tests.
404	
405	### Cross-cutting
406	Concurrency model (workers-per-pool, in-flight burn reservation); route observability
407	(chosen route, snapshot age/source/confidence, scarcity score, fallback reason);
408	simulation/replay harness before any live routing change. All thresholds are
409	data-tunable, NOT spec-locked constants.

662	// Resolve runs the engine end-to-end and returns a Decision.
663	//
664	// The engine:
665	//  1. Enumerates (harness, provider, model) candidates from inputs.
666	//  2. Applies gating (capability, override, model-pin, surface).
667	//  3. Scores per policy with cooldown demotion + perf bias.
668	//  4. Sorts viable → score → cost → locality → name.
669	//  5. Returns the top viable candidate with the full ranked list.
670	//
671	// Returns an error only when no viable candidate exists.
672	func Resolve(req Request, in Inputs) (*Decision, error) {
673		if in.Now.IsZero() {
674			in.Now = time.Now()
675		}
676	
677		// Safe mode: force default (middle-tier) policy and disable local mixin.
678		// Phase 2+ quota economics and local speculative routing are bypassed
679		// regardless of what the caller requested.
680		if in.SafeMode {
681			req.Policy = "default"
682		}
683	
684		policyName, err := canonicalPolicy(req.Policy)
685		if err != nil {
686			return &Decision{}, err
687		}
688		req.Policy = policyName
689		if err := validateRequirements(req); err != nil {
690			return &Decision{}, err
691		}
692	
693		canonicalHarness := req.Harness
694		if canonicalHarness == "local" {
695			canonicalHarness = "fiz"
696		}
697		if err := explicitPinError(req, in); err != nil {
698			return &Decision{}, err
699		}
700	
701		var ranked []rankedCandidate
702		for _, h := range in.Harnesses {
703			// TestOnly harnesses (script/virtual) only reachable via explicit override.
704			if h.TestOnly && canonicalHarness != h.Name {
705				continue
706			}
707			// Automatic profile/tier routing is restricted to harnesses with full
708			// coverage. Explicit Harness pins can still use experimental/ad-hoc
709			// harnesses.
710			if canonicalHarness == "" && !h.AutoRoutingEligible {
711				continue
712			}
713			// Hard harness override: skip non-matching harnesses.
714			if canonicalHarness != "" && canonicalHarness != h.Name {
715				continue
716			}
717			entries := buildHarnessCandidates(h, req, in)
718			ranked = append(ranked, entries...)
719		}
720	
721		// Compute scores for candidates that survived the primary gates. A later
722		// max-power exclusion pass may turn some of these scored candidates
723		// ineligible so the trace can retain power evidence without letting an
724		// overpowered route win automatic selection.
725		for i := range ranked {
726			if !ranked[i].out.Eligible {
727				continue
728			}
729			ranked[i].out.Score = scorePolicy(req.Policy, ranked[i].internal)
730			ranked[i].out.ScoreComponents = scoreComponents(req.Policy, ranked[i].internal)
731			ranked[i].out.Reason = fmt.Sprintf("policy=%s; score=%.1f", req.Policy, ranked[i].out.Score)
732		}
733		applyMaxPowerExclusion(ranked, req)
734		applyModelPinSubscriptionPreference(ranked, req, in)
735		neutralCost, hasKnownCost := neutralKnownCost(ranked)
736	
737		// Sort: eligible first, then descending score, then cost, then locality,
738		// then alphabetical.
739		sort.SliceStable(ranked, func(i, j int) bool {
740			ei, ej := ranked[i].out.Eligible, ranked[j].out.Eligible
741			if ei != ej {
742				return ei
743			}
744			if !ei {
745				return ranked[i].out.Harness < ranked[j].out.Harness
746			}
747			if ranked[i].out.Score != ranked[j].out.Score {
748				return ranked[i].out.Score > ranked[j].out.Score
749			}
750			if hasKnownCost {
751				ci := candidateCostTieValue(ranked[i], neutralCost)
752				cj := candidateCostTieValue(ranked[j], neutralCost)
753				if ci != cj {
754					return ci < cj
755				}
756			}
757			// Locality tiebreak: prefer local cost-class.
758			li := costClassRank[ranked[i].internal.CostClass] == 0
759			lj := costClassRank[ranked[j].internal.CostClass] == 0
760			if li != lj {
761				return li
762			}
763			if sameLocalEndpointGroup(ranked[i].internal, ranked[j].internal) {
764				if ranked[i].internal.EndpointSaturated != ranked[j].internal.EndpointSaturated {
765					return !ranked[i].internal.EndpointSaturated
766				}
767				if ranked[i].internal.EndpointLoad != ranked[j].internal.EndpointLoad {
768					return ranked[i].internal.EndpointLoad < ranked[j].internal.EndpointLoad
769				}
770			}
771			if ranked[i].out.Harness != ranked[j].out.Harness {
772				return ranked[i].out.Harness < ranked[j].out.Harness
773			}
774			return ranked[i].out.Provider < ranked[j].out.Provider
775		})
776	
777		out := make([]Candidate, len(ranked))
778		for i := range ranked {
779			out[i] = ranked[i].out
780		}
781	
782		for i := range out {
783			if out[i].Eligible {
784				return &Decision{
785					Harness:        out[i].Harness,
786					Provider:       out[i].Provider,
787					Endpoint:       out[i].Endpoint,
788					ServerInstance: out[i].ServerInstance,
789					Model:          out[i].Model,
790					Reason:         fmt.Sprintf("policy=%s; score=%.1f", req.Policy, out[i].Score),
791					Candidates:     out,
792				}, nil
793			}
794		}
795		if quotaErr := allProvidersQuotaExhaustedError(ranked); quotaErr != nil {
796			return &Decision{Candidates: out}, quotaErr
797		}
798		if requested := requestedModelIntent(req); requested != "" && req.Provider == "" && canonicalHarness == "" && hasLiveDiscoveryCandidates(ranked) {
799			return &Decision{Candidates: out}, fmt.Errorf("no live endpoint offers a match for %s", requested)
800		}
801		if missingRequirement := missingPolicyRequirement(req, out); missingRequirement != "" {
802			return &Decision{Candidates: out}, &ErrPolicyRequirementUnsatisfied{
803				Policy:      req.Policy,
804				Requirement: missingRequirement,
805				Rejected:    len(out),
806			}
807		}
808	
809		// For unpinned requests with no viable candidates at the current policy,
810		// attempt escalation to the next policy in the ladder before returning
811		// the error. Hard-pinned requests (with Model/Provider/Harness) must not
812		// escalate — they fail with the original no-viable error.
813		if isUnpinnedRequest(req) {
814			nextPolicy := nextPolicyInLadder(req.Policy)
815			if nextPolicy != "" {
816				probe := req
817				probe.Policy = nextPolicy
818				if dec, err := Resolve(probe, in); err == nil && dec != nil && dec.Harness != "" {
819					return dec, nil
820				}
821			}
822		}
823	
824		return &Decision{Candidates: out}, noViableCandidateError(req, len(out))
825	}

861	// applyModelPinSubscriptionPreference enforces that an explicit --model pin
862	// (with no --harness/--provider override) is honored by a configured
863	// subscription harness whose SupportedModels covers the pinned model,
864	// rather than by a provider-routed fallback such as fiz/openrouter.

867	// have," a catalog-known openrouter route for the same concrete model can
868	// otherwise outscore the subscription harness on perf/cost signals and
869	// silently switch the dispatch destination to a per-token provider that
870	// likely lacks an auth header. The preference only fires when at least one
871	// subscription-harness candidate is still eligible and lists the pin in
872	// its SupportedModels — if no subscription advertises the model, the
873	// engine falls back to fiz/openrouter as before.
874	func applyModelPinSubscriptionPreference(ranked []rankedCandidate, req Request, in Inputs) {
875		if req.Model == "" || req.Harness != "" || req.Provider != "" {
876			return
877		}
878		hasEligibleSubscriptionMatch := false
879		for i := range ranked {
880			if !ranked[i].out.Eligible || !ranked[i].internal.IsSubscription {
881				continue
882			}
883			h, ok := findHarness(in.Harnesses, ranked[i].out.Harness)
884			if !ok || len(h.SupportedModels) == 0 {
885				continue
886			}
887			if harnessSupportsModel(h.SupportedModels, req.Model) {
888				hasEligibleSubscriptionMatch = true
889				break
890			}
891		}
892		if !hasEligibleSubscriptionMatch {
893			return
894		}
895		for i := range ranked {
896			if !ranked[i].out.Eligible || ranked[i].internal.IsSubscription {
897				continue
898			}
899			ranked[i].out.Eligible = false
900			ranked[i].out.FilterReason = FilterReasonScoredBelowTop
901			ranked[i].out.Reason = fmt.Sprintf("model pin %q satisfied by configured subscription harness; non-subscription fallback suppressed", req.Model)
902		}
903	}

918	// at least one routing candidate was rejected solely because its provider is
919	// in the quota_exhausted state and no other candidate was eligible. The set

922	// passed every other gate). When that set is empty the existing
923	// no-viable / no-profile-candidate / live-discovery errors describe the
924	// failure more precisely.

928		var earliest time.Time
929		for _, c := range ranked {
930			if c.quotaExhaustedRetryAfter.IsZero() {
931				continue
932			}
933			name := c.out.Provider
934			if name == "" {
935				name = c.out.Harness
936			}
937			if _, dup := seen[name]; !dup {
938				seen[name] = struct{}{}
939				exhausted = append(exhausted, name)
940			}
941			if earliest.IsZero() || c.quotaExhaustedRetryAfter.Before(earliest) {
942				earliest = c.quotaExhaustedRetryAfter
943			}
944		}
945		if len(exhausted) == 0 {
946			return nil
947		}
948		return &ErrAllProvidersQuotaExhausted{
949			RetryAfter:         earliest,
950			ExhaustedProviders: exhausted,
951		}
